newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.S. pilot in Indonesia on Earhart tribute trip.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pilot in Indonesia on Earhart tribute trip.

text.p: American pilot Linda Finch arrived in Indonesia's capital Jakarta on Tuesday on the latest leg of her bid to complete the around-the-world journey attempted by Amelia Earhart 60 years ago.

Finch landed at the Halim Perdana Kusuma airbase from Singapore in a 1935 Lockheed Electra 10E, the same model used by Earhart, who vanished between New Guinea and Howland Island in the Pacific in 1937.
Dozens of reporters, photographers and cameramen rushed toward the aircraft as it approached the terminal building, elbowing out dancers gathered for a ceremonial welcome.
Finch did not speak to reporters and the press was barred from the ceremony conducted later.

The plane, one of only two remaining, was painstakingly restored for "World Flight 1997", a $4.5 million project. Finch's journey will last two and a half months, cover a total distance of 26,748 miles (43,045 km) and span five continents.
Finch set out on March 17 from the same hangar in Oakland, California, from which Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan departed.

She is scheduled to fly to Surabaya in East Java on Wednesday before continuing the journey to Australia and then traverse the New Guinea to Howland Island leg, during which Earhart's plane disappeared on July 2, 1937.
Finch aims to complete the journey by returning to Oakland in mid-May.
